79f2556f: What Coodoo is, and what it is not
ce8fe3c9: Coodoo is software by CentreBrain that runs on your own computer and organises AI coding agents as a team: it turns your idea into goals and tasks, lets the agents build, test and review, and puts the result on GitHub. The AI itself is not part of Coodoo. It comes from third-party services: Claude Code from Anthropic and Codex from OpenAI. You take out and pay for those services yourself; their own terms and privacy policies apply to them.
8699ed77: AI models predict text; they do not understand your project the way a person does. Code can fail to work, work only in some cases, or do something other than you asked. An explanation can be wrong or simply invented, while sounding convincing.
9c529b43: AI can write code with weaknesses: a login that can be bypassed, data that is visible to the wrong people, or a package with a known vulnerability. Coodoo checks for common problems, but no check finds everything. Be extra careful with apps that handle accounts, payments or personal data.
8710e78f: The agents change files in your project, and the app they build can change data, for example in a database. Coodoo keeps your work in Git and on GitHub and never rewrites history, but a mistake can still remove or damage something. Keep backups of anything you cannot lose, and never let the team work on real production data.
324a7ffd: AI that works on its own
d986e44e: With the autopilot, the agents run commands on your computer without asking you each time: installing packages, building, testing and starting your app. Coodoo limits what they can do (they write only in your project folder, cannot reach your GitHub login, and some actions are always refused), but these limits cannot rule out every risk. The app the team builds runs with your own rights when Coodoo starts it.
3b6bcf60: What the agents read, such as your code, your messages and screenshots, is sent to the AI service you use (Anthropic or OpenAI) and processed under their terms. Do not put other people’s personal data, passwords or confidential business information in a chat or a project unless you are allowed to share it with those services. Coodoo keeps keys from its vault out of commits and logs, but cannot see everything you type.
a4355ac4: AI work uses your subscription’s limits or, with an API key, money per use. The costs Coodoo shows are estimates. Keep an eye on your usage with Anthropic and OpenAI themselves.
c6916956: Code written by AI can resemble existing code, and the packages it uses come with their own licenses. Check that you may use what is in your project the way you intend, especially before you sell or publish it.
9bf17100: Laws and rules for your app
4f7a6c61: If your app processes personal data, takes payments or uses AI itself, rules may apply to you, such as the GDPR (AVG) in Europe. Coodoo cannot judge whether your app meets them. That remains your responsibility.
777e2159: Coodoo depends on services of others, such as Anthropic, OpenAI and GitHub. They can change, become unavailable or change their prices and limits. CentreBrain has no control over that.
0d3b5d11: Do not use software the team made for medical, financial, legal or safety-critical purposes without a thorough check by a qualified professional.
27dcd04c: What Coodoo does to limit the risks
a5c5b390: Safety rules that are always on: your repository is never deleted or made public, history is never rewritten, and keys stay secret.
10ff7916: With two agents, one builds and the other reviews; Coodoo also starts your app and checks it, and scans for known security problems.
d1ef6549: Work only reaches your main branch through the steps of your flow.
a77360bf: More on the safety rules and in the manual.

45ce3f95: Keep backups, and work with test data, not real customer data.

4114f1b8: Ask an expert when your app handles money, health or personal data.

card.claude-code-and-codex.title: With Claude Code and Codex
card.claude-code-and-codex.text: What Coodoo adds to the agents you use.
autopilot.pt1: Phases you switch on and off yourself
autopilot.pt2: Pause and continue at any moment; nothing is lost
autopilot.pt3: Every step in the run log, in plain words
autopilot.pt4: A yellow card when it needs you, such as for a command only you may run
autopilot.step1: Describe your idea in the chat, in your own words.
autopilot.step2: Agree on a goal: the agent asks what it needs to know and proposes one.
autopilot.step3: Start the autopilot. The team makes a plan and splits it into tasks.
autopilot.step4: Task by task, one agent builds and the tests run.
autopilot.step5: The other agent reviews, and Coodoo starts your app to see whether it works.
autopilot.step6: The finished goal lands on your development branch on GitHub.
autopilot.q1: Can I stop the autopilot at any time?
autopilot.a1: Yes. Pause it and continue later, or stop it. The work so far stays on its branch.
autopilot.q2: Does it keep working while I’m away?
autopilot.a2: Yes, as long as your computer is on and Coodoo is open. It keeps the computer from going to sleep while it works.
autopilot.a3: The run log says what went wrong. The team tries to fix it; when it needs you, a yellow card tells you what to do.
autopilot.s1h: A team that keeps going without you
autopilot.s1p: Every goal goes through the same phases as in a real software team: research, design, planning, development, review and delivery. You choose which phases are on and which agent takes which role. With “Keep working” on, the team even thinks up sensible next goals itself.
autopilot.h1: The autopilot: from idea to working app.
autopilot.lead: Coodoo turns your idea into goals and tasks and lets an AI team work through them on its own: plan, build, test, review and deliver to GitHub. You watch, pause or step in whenever you like.
autopilot.s2p: The autopilot runs on your own computer, with your own Claude and/or ChatGPT subscription. While it works, Coodoo keeps your computer awake and shows how much of your subscription you use. Its safety rules are always on.
ai-code-review.pt1: The reviewer approves or asks for specific changes
ai-code-review.pt2: The builder fixes them, for as many rounds as you allow
ai-code-review.pt3: Coodoo starts your app, looks at its pages and takes screenshots
ai-code-review.pt4: Scans for leaked keys and known vulnerable packages
ai-code-review.step1: The developer agent builds the task and writes tests.
ai-code-review.step2: Coodoo runs the tests and starts your app to look at it.
ai-code-review.step3: The reviewer reads the changes and the app report.
ai-code-review.step4: Approved: the task is committed in your name. Changes needed: the developer fixes them and the reviewer looks again.
ai-code-review.q1: Do I need both Claude and ChatGPT?
ai-code-review.a1: No, one is enough. With both, one builds and the other reviews, which catches more mistakes.
ai-code-review.q2: Can I switch the review off?
ai-code-review.a2: Yes. Every phase can be switched on or off per project. We recommend keeping the review on.
ai-code-review.q3: Does the AI review replace my own check?
ai-code-review.a3: No. It catches a lot, but AI can make mistakes. Look at and try what the team made before you use it.
ai-code-review.s1p: Two different AI models make different mistakes, so they catch more of each other’s. The reviewer reads what changed, the test results and the report of the running app, and only then decides.
ai-code-review.h1: One AI builds. The other checks.
ai-code-review.lead: With Claude Code and Codex together, every task gets a second pair of eyes. The reviewer approves the work or asks for changes, and Coodoo starts your app to see whether it really works.
ai-code-review.s2p: One subscription is enough: then the same AI does the review, in a separate step with a fresh look. Two different AIs catch more, which is why Coodoo works best with both.
safety.pt1: Your repository is never deleted, archived, transferred or made public
safety.pt2: No force pushes, no rewritten history, no deleted branches or tags
safety.pt3: Keys live encrypted in a vault, never in a commit, and show as REDACTED in every log
safety.pt4: The agents write only in your project folder and cannot reach your GitHub login
safety.pt5: Only pre-approved actions on GitHub, and commits in your name
safety.pt6: Work reaches your main branch only through the steps of your flow
safety.step1: An agent or command tries something a rule forbids.
safety.step2: Coodoo stops it before anything changes.
safety.step3: The goal stops or skips that step, and you get a notification.
safety.step4: Everything a failsafe stopped is kept in a log you can read in Settings.
safety.q1: Can I switch the failsafes off?
safety.a1: No. They are always on, also for you. That way a mistake can never undo them.
safety.q2: Can the AI see my passwords and keys?
safety.a2: Keys go into Coodoo’s encrypted vault and are blanked out in logs. The agents get no GitHub login; your app gets a key only when you hand it over.
safety.q3: Where can I see what was stopped?
safety.a3: In Settings → Failsafes, with what was tried, when and why it was stopped.
safety.s1p: These rules protect your code, your accounts and your keys, also when an agent makes a mistake or misunderstands a goal.
safety.h1: The agents work on their own. Within hard limits.
safety.lead: Coodoo’s failsafes stop risky actions before they happen. They are always on: no goal, agent or button can switch them off.
safety.s2p: The failsafes make working with AI a lot safer, but they cannot rule out every risk: AI can make mistakes, and the app the team builds runs with your own rights. Read the disclaimer and the risks of AI.
github-flow.pt1: Every goal on its own branch, cleaned up afterwards
github-flow.pt2: Commits in your name, never in the AI’s
github-flow.pt3: Promote to the next branch with one click
github-flow.pt4: Releases with a changelog in plain words
github-flow.step1: A goal gets its own branch.
github-flow.step2: Each approved task is committed there in your name.
github-flow.step3: The finished goal is combined, tested and reviewed, and goes to development.
github-flow.step4: You promote it to staging and main, through the checks of your flow.
github-flow.q1: Do I need to know Git?
github-flow.a1: No. Coodoo handles branches, commits and pull requests for you.
github-flow.q2: Can I use an existing repository?
github-flow.a2: Yes. Open or clone a repository you already have; Coodoo works with it as it is.
github-flow.q3: What if I work on two computers?
github-flow.a3: Get the latest work on the other computer with one click. An agent checks both sides first, so nothing is lost.
github-flow.s1p: You set the branches your work goes through, such as development → staging → main. Coodoo never skips a step, opens pull requests where a branch is protected, and keeps everything in your own GitHub account.
github-flow.h1: Neat on GitHub. Nothing reaches main untested.
github-flow.lead: Coodoo works with Git and GitHub the way a professional team does, so you don’t have to: every goal on its own branch, delivered to development, and promoted to staging and main through checks you choose.
github-flow.s2p: You don’t have to know what a branch or a merge is. Coodoo explains what happens in plain words, and asks you only when a decision is yours, such as before something goes to main.
programs.pt1: Choose versions, such as PHP 8.4 or Node 22, and a standard per language
programs.pt2: Patches checked every day and installed by themselves
programs.pt3: Laravel without Laravel Herd: PHP and Composer included
programs.pt4: Coodoo’s own MySQL and PostgreSQL, with a database for each project
programs.pt5: Laravel Herd and Docker still work, if you use them
programs.step2: Coodoo sees what it needs, from files such as package.json or composer.json.
programs.step3: What is missing is installed from the official source and checked.
programs.step4: Your app starts with the right versions, and its database is ready.
programs.a1: No. Everything goes into Coodoo’s own folder and only Coodoo uses it. Your PATH and your own terminal stay as they are.
programs.q2: Do I need Laravel Herd or Docker?
programs.a2: No. Coodoo installs PHP, Composer and the databases itself. If you already use Herd or Docker, Coodoo works with them.
programs.q3: Where do the programs come from?
programs.a3: From fixed, known sources such as nodejs.org, Eclipse Temurin, python-build-standalone, static-php-cli, windows.php.net, mysql.com and Maven Central, each download checked with a checksum.
programs.s1p: A bit like Docker, without the containers: the programs live in Coodoo’s own folder, and only Coodoo uses them. The agents, the terminal in Coodoo and your running app get the right version, and your own setup stays as it was.
programs.h1: Languages and databases, without the installing.
programs.lead: Node.js, Python, Java, PHP, MySQL and PostgreSQL: Coodoo installs the versions your project needs in its own folder, checked with a checksum and without an admin password. Nothing on the rest of your computer changes.
programs.s2p: It works on macOS and Windows. On Windows, PHP needs the Microsoft Visual C++ Runtime, which most PCs already have; if it is missing, Coodoo says where to get it.

claude-code-and-codex.a2: Claude (Pro or Max) for Claude Code and/or ChatGPT (Plus or Pro) for Codex. One is enough; with both, one builds and the other reviews.

claude-code-and-codex.a3: Yes. Coodoo uses the normal programs, so you can keep using them in your own terminal as well.
claude-code-and-codex.s1p: On their own, the agents wait for your next command in a terminal, and you arrange Git, testing and safety yourself. Coodoo turns them into a team you talk to in plain words.
